items.claim: The cluster's core evidence (a repeated tongue-noun at the 12:18/12:19 seam) is byte-accurate, but device_notes misreports the book's sword-root sweep as the chapter's five sword-class occurrences, wrong on both scope and count.
items.evidence: The shared token verifies at byte tier: 12:18's B-colon carries וּלְשׁ֖וֹן חֲכָמִ֣ים; 12:19 closes on לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר -- same lexeme repeated, same pointing, genuinely a shared object, so the cluster's stated glue holds. But device_notes' digit claim does not: sweep.py --skel on the sword root returns 5 verses BOOK-WIDE (Prov.5.4, 12.18, 17.1, 25.18, 30.14), not 5 within chapter 12, which contains only this one occurrence (12:18). Of those 5, only 4 are sword-class -- 5:4 כְּחֶ֣רֶב, 12:18 חָ֑רֶב, 25:18 וְ֭חֶרֶב, 30:14 חֲרָב֣וֹת -- the 5th, 17:1's חֲ֭רֵבָה (dry-morsel), is the homograph the row itself calls distinct. "The chapter's five sword-class occurrences" therefore both misplaces the scope (book, not chapter) and over-counts the class by folding the homograph in.
tier_citations: byte (collate.py GREEN: oshb:Prov.12.18, oshb:Prov.12.19, oshb:Prov.5.4, oshb:Prov.17.1, oshb:Prov.25.18, oshb:Prov.30.14)
skeleton sweep (sweep.py --skel on the sword root: 5 verses book-wide, per TOOLKIT.md sword/dry-morsel hazard entry)

items.claim: 12:20's opening abstract noun genuinely repeats 12:17's clause-final noun at byte tier, and 12:20 shares no token with the intervening 12:18-12:19, so both the cited link and the rejected pairing are accurate.
items.evidence: 12:17 ends מִרְמָֽה; 12:20 opens מִ֭רְמָה -- identical pointed noun (absolute, not construct), confirmed at byte tier, three verses apart as the row states. A skeleton-token adjacency check of 12:19 against 12:20 (consonantal_index.json, len>=2 tokens) returns no overlap, matching the row's rejected_alternative that 12:19's tongue/falsehood vocabulary does not recur here.
tier_citations: skeleton adjacency check (consonantal_index.json, Prov.12.19 vs Prov.12.20: no shared token)

items.claim: observed_substrate_signals asserts the A- and B-cola of 12:21 pivot on the same evil-root noun, but the two nouns are unrelated roots -- a translation-dependent claim that only looks true in English (both gloss as "evil"); the row also mislabels the verse's genuine catchword with 12:20.
items.evidence: 12:21's A-colon noun is אָ֑וֶן and its B-colon noun is רָֽע -- distinct skeletons (aleph-vav-nun vs. resh-ayin), not the same root under any pointing or allography; the "same evil-root noun" claim does not survive a byte check and only holds if both are collapsed to the shared English gloss "evil." Separately, a skeleton adjacency sweep (consonantal_index.json) shows 12:20 and 12:21 ARE linked by a genuine repeated token: 12:20 ends חֹ֣רְשֵׁי רָ֑ע and 12:21 ends on the identical word רָֽע -- the real catchword sits between the two verses, not within 12:21's own cola. The row's rejected_alternative calls this "a different sense-slot" rather than naming the identical repeated word, so the one real inter-verse catchword at this seam is under-disclosed while a false intra-verse one is asserted as evidence.
tier_citations: skeleton adjacency sweep (consonantal_index.json: Prov.12.20<->Prov.12.21 shared final token)

items.claim: The disclosed lexical crux behind WEB's rendering is a genuine, honestly-hedged textual difficulty; the antithetic frame the row keeps is unaffected by which construal is preferred, and no morphology layer is staged to settle it.
items.evidence: 12:26 opens יָתֵ֣ר מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ צַדִּ֑יק -- confirmed at byte tier. The row does not overclaim a resolution and explicitly flags that no morphology layer is staged for this extract (matching TOOLKIT.md's own disclosed limitation), while correctly noting the antithetic shape (waw-adversative into the wicked/wicked's-way clause) holds regardless of the crux.

items.claim: The hunting-image reading of 12:27's A-colon and the disclosed non-bridge to 12:25's emotional vocabulary both check out at byte/skeleton tier.
items.evidence: 12:27 opens לֹא יַחֲרֹ֣ךְ רְמִיָּ֣ה -- confirmed at byte tier. A skeleton adjacency check of 12:25 against 12:27 (checked as the row's named rejected pairing) returns no shared content token, consistent with the row's claim that no vocabulary bridges the two.
tier_citations: skeleton check (consonantal_index.json: Prov.12.25 vs Prov.12.27, no shared token)

items.claim: 13:3's own asyndeton (no waw anywhere in the verse) is byte-accurate, but the row cites 12:24 as a matching chapter-12 asyndetic verse when 12:24 is in fact syndetic -- it has an overt waw joining its cola.
items.evidence: 13:3 in full: נֹצֵ֣ר פִּ֭יו שֹׁמֵ֣ר נַפְשׁ֑וֹ פֹּשֵׂ֥ק שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו מְחִתָּה לֽוֹ -- no waw at any position, genuinely asyndetic. But 12:24 in full: יַד חָרוּצִ֥ים תִּמְשׁ֑וֹל ו֝רְמִיָּ֗ה תִּהְיֶ֥ה לָמַֽס -- the B-colon opens with a waw-prefixed noun, ו֝רְמִיָּ֗ה, so 12:24 is syndetic, not an asyndetic parallel to 13:3. The verse that actually matches 13:3's construction is 12:5: מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת צַדִּיקִ֣ים מִשְׁפָּ֑ט תַּחְבֻּל֖וֹת רְשָׁעִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה -- two juxtaposed noun-clauses with no connector at all -- which the row also cites correctly; only the 12:24 half of the citation is wrong.

items.claim: The shared appetite/soul noun across 13:3 and 13:4 is byte-confirmed, and the row's own disclosure of it as thin, non-cluster-worthy vocabulary (rather than silently ignoring it) matches the cross-seam cohesion standard.
items.evidence: 13:3 carries נַפְשׁ֑וֹ as its object; 13:4's A-colon carries the identical suffixed form נַפְשׁ֣וֹ as its subject -- same word, same pointing, confirmed at byte tier. The row discloses this explicitly in device_notes rather than leaving it as an undisclosed cross-seam device, and its reasoning for not clustering (common vocabulary, no shared construction) is consistent with the range's general catchword-adjacency weakness.

items.claim: The doubled there-is-with-ellipsis reading of 13:7 is byte-accurate -- the particle occurs exactly once, at the verse's opening -- and the synthetic/paradoxical parallelism label (rather than antithetic) correctly fits the mirrored-reversal content.
items.evidence: 13:7 in full: יֵ֣שׁ מִ֭תְעַשֵּׁר וְאֵ֣ין כֹּ֑ל מִ֝תְרוֹשֵׁ֗שׁ וְה֣וֹן רָֽב -- יֵ֣שׁ occurs exactly once, at the verse opening; the B-colon has no second occurrence of it and no adversative waw marking a righteous/wicked class contrast, matching the row's ellipsis claim and its parallelism-class label.
